target_customer: Startups and software companies in the US, UK and Australia that can claim R&D tax credits (named customers include Edexia, Lewi Software, Fluer, Knowz, Desygner)
problem: R&D tax credit claims are labor heavy and rely on consultants and surveys, so many eligible companies skip them or overpay.
business_model: tax services firm using AI, likely fee based on claims (fee structure not found)
product_category: AI-native tax services, R&D tax credits

founders.name: Rachel Huang
previous_startups: Serial founder, 4 startups per YC profile (names not given)
founders.background_notes: Former professional tennis player per YC page.

founders.name: William Mahon
prior_employers: a high-frequency trading firm (low-level systems engineer)

competitors.name: Boast.ai
competitors.what: AI R&D credit platform with expert services
competitors.traction_then: says it has secured over $150M in credits

competitors.name: Neo.Tax
competitors.what: AI software for R&D credits and software capitalization
competitors.funding_then: about $13M total per a profile page (unverified)

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting to GitHub, Jira, Drive and accounting tools and drafting Form 6765 and studies is standard integration plus LLM work with expert review.

defensibility.rationale: Several AI and incumbent firms offer the same service; value comes from execution and expert review, not hard to copy tech.

market_need_then: R&D credits are widely underclaimed and Section 174 changes raised attention; a 2025 piece warns about AI pop-up tax firms, showing active but contested demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses claimkit.co, not .com; claimkit.com belonged to an unrelated Kansas insurance software company of the same name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and benefit focused, e.g. R&D tax credits, maximized on autopilot.

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with an older ClaimKit insurance software company with registered trademarks; no brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: ClaimKit is a Fall 2026 YC company pitching an AI-native tax firm for R&D credits. It is too early for an outcome. It claims more than 80 credits claimed on its site (company claim), but faces Boast and Neo.Tax and shares its name with an older company.
notes: Funding: Dealroom lists a Brisbane based ClaimKit with a $125k seed and founders Rachel Huang, Ben Ashdown and William Mahon (single aggregator; the YC page does not list Ashdown), so unverified and not recorded as a round. ClaimKit Inc of Kansas ($1.8M in 2016) is a different company. Competitor sources dated 2025 and 2026 around the Fall 2026 batch. The site's $100M+ claim is unclear and not used.
